notes: run.py builds a repo per run from `fixture`, runs `prompt` with `claude -p`, then copies the reports from ~/.ai/<repo-slug>/reviews/ to outputs/reviews/, writes outputs/git-state.txt, and deletes ~/.ai/<repo-slug>/. `{name}` in a prompt is the `name=` value from the fixture.

common_checks.text: Does not call the host, push, or send a notification directly
The local branch and the working tree do not change
Does not use the fast-forward fetch of fetch-gitlab-mr.sh
Starts the review watch of !11 in the background
Starts the watch again with no --fresh

evals.name: watch-amend
evals.prompt:
{intro} The review watch of !11 runs.

The background watch task stopped with exit 0. Output:
```
{event}
```
evals.expected_output: The session fetches, runs git-interdiff.sh, and reviews only the change: M1 is fixed, and short() fails for names shorter than 3 characters. It adds an update to the report, reports under Needs you, and starts the watch again.

checks.text: Does not review the full MR again
The report has an update with the substring finding
Reply has the new finding under Needs you and tells that M1 is fixed

evals.name: watch-rebase-noop
evals.prompt:
{intro} The review watch of !11 runs.

The background watch task stopped with exit 0. Output:
```
{event}
```
evals.expected_output: The session runs git-interdiff.sh, gets no output, and reports one Info line: rebased, no content change. No review, no update in the report.

checks.text: Does not review the full MR again
Reply tells that the push has no content change

evals.name: watch-comments
evals.expected_output: The reply of @anna is wrong: the default locale changes how ASCII 'i' becomes upper case. The session puts its assessment and a proposed response under Needs you, as one item. The comment of @bob, the failed pipeline, and the approval are under Info. No retry, no reply.

checks.text: Reply has Needs you for @anna with an assessment, and Info for @bob and the pipeline
The comment and its thread are one item

evals.name: watch-resolved
evals.prompt:
{intro} The review watch of !11 runs.

The background watch task stopped with exit 0. Output:
```
{"kind":"resolved","iid":11,"title":"Add Tag model","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/notes/app/-/merge_requests/11#note_801","actor":"anna","detail":"Use uppercase(Locale.ROOT) here.","branch":"tags-model","path":"app/src/main/kotlin/notes/Tag.kt","line":6}
```
evals.expected_output: The MR head did not change, so no commit fixes the thread. The session puts it under Needs you as resolved with no fix.

checks.text: Reply has the thread under Needs you as resolved with no fix

evals.name: watch-start-behind
evals.prompt: {intro} You gave the review reply. Start the watch.
evals.expected_output: The session starts the review watch, fetches, and finds that the author pushed during the review. It handles the push as a pushed event: git-interdiff.sh, a review of the change, an update in the report.

checks.text: The report has an update with the substring finding

evals.name: watch-resolved-after-push
evals.expected_output: The push fixes M1, and @anna resolved the M1 thread. The session handles the push first. It compares the thread with the change since the full review, finds the fix, and puts the thread under Info, not as resolved with no fix.

checks.text: Reply does not put the fixed thread under resolved with no fix
